title: Milei Overhauls SIDE Intelligence Services by Decree: Agents Gain Arrest Powers, Operations Report to Karina Milei
detail: President Javier Milei published a sweeping overhaul of SIDE (Secretaría de Inteligencia del Estado) via presidential decree in the Official Gazette on June 6, 2026. The reform grants intelligence agents extraordinary new powers previously reserved for law enforcement: agents may now arrest individuals on the spot without a judicial warrant in defined national security circumstances. The decree classifies all SIDE operations as 'covert' by default and grants the agency authority to request the armed forces perform interior intelligence tasks — a boundary traditionally prohibited under Argentine law to prevent a return to Dirty War-era militarized domestic surveillance. Critically, the restructured intelligence apparatus now reports to the General Secretariat of the Presidency, headed by Milei's sister Karina Milei, rather than to a minister with congressional oversight. A cross-party group of Chamber of Deputies members issued a formal warning that the reform 'opens the door to surveillance practices incompatible with the rule of law' and called for emergency hearings to assess whether the decree violated the Intelligence Services Law 25,520 enacted after Argentina's return to democracy. Human rights organizations — including CELS and Madres de Plaza de Mayo — raised alarm about the risk of recreating structures associated with the 1976–1983 military dictatorship.

media.caption: Milei's SIDE intelligence overhaul grants arrest powers to agents and places spy agency under Karina Milei
